name: Rhodesia 1965-1979
description: Rhodesia was a self-declared independent state in southern Africa from 1965 to 1979, following the Unilateral Declaration of Independence (UDI) from the United Kingdom led by Prime Minister Ian Smith. The government was dominated by the white minority and was not internationally recognized. After years of guerrilla warfare and international sanctions, the state transitioned in 1979 to Zimbabwe-Rhodesia and later became internationally recognized as Zimbabwe in 1980.

name: Zimbabwe 1980-Present
description: Zimbabwe became independent in 1980 after the end of white-minority rule in Rhodesia and the Lancaster House Agreement. In 1979, Rhodesia briefly became Zimbabwe Rhodesia, a transitional state with limited recognition before British-administered elections. The country then emerged as the Republic of Zimbabwe, initially led by Robert Mugabe. Since independence it has experienced political turmoil, land reforms, economic crises, and periods of hyperinflation while remaining a sovereign state in southern Africa.

name: Imerina Kingdom (1540-1787)
description: Founded by Andriamanelo, the Imerina Kingdom began as a network of fortified clan hilltop settlements. This period focuses on internal consolidation, the introduction of ironwork, and the development of irrigated rice agriculture. It concludes in 1787 because this marks the end of a long era of internal fragmentation and civil war between four rival sub-kingdoms, just before Andrianampoinimerina ascended the throne to launch his campaign for total national reunification.

name: Kingdom of Madagascar (1840-1897 AD)
description: By 1840, the Kingdom had reached its maximum territorial extent, unifying most of the island under Merina rule. This period was characterized by intense diplomatic efforts to maintain independence from European powers, the official adoption of Christianity in 1869, and modernization attempts. It concludes in 1897 following the French military invasion and the subsequent abolition of the monarchy, which saw the last sovereign, Queen Ranavalona III, forced into exile.

name: Republic of Madagascar (1960-present)
description: After 63 years of colonial rule, Madagascar regained its independence from France on June 26, 1960. The new Republic transitioned through various political phases, from the pro-French First Republic to a socialist era in the 1970s, and finally to its current democratic framework. The nation remains a unique cultural bridge between Africa and Southeast Asia.

name: Kingdom of Antongil (1771-1786 AD)
description: A short-lived state established in northeastern Madagascar by the adventurer Maurice Benyovszky. Proclaimed 'Ampansacabe' (Supreme King) by local Betsimisaraka chiefs in 1776, Benyovszky attempted to create an independent trade empire. The kingdom featured a capital city, Louisbourg, and resisted French colonial oversight until Benyovszky's death in 1786 during a skirmish with French forces sent to dismantle his administration.

name: Kingdom of Menabe (1610-1822 AD)
description: The foundation of the Sakalava Empire, Menabe emerged around 1610 on the west coast of Madagascar. It became the island's first major military power by acquiring firearms through maritime trade. Under King Andriandahifotsy, it dominated the western plains and forced neighboring highland kingdoms into tributary status. The kingdom maintained its political core until 1834, when it was largely integrated into the Merina Empire after decades of conflict.

name: Kingdom of Boina (1690-1824 AD)
description: Boina originated around 1690 as a major secession from the Menabe Kingdom following a succession dispute. Prince Andriamandisoarivo migrated north with his followers and firearms to establish this independent Sakalava state, which dominated Indian Ocean trade through the port of Majunga. The kingdom's independence ended in 1824 when King Radama I of Imerina launched a massive military campaign, capturing Majunga and annexing Boina into the unified Kingdom of Madagascar, effectively ending Sakalava regional hegemony.

name: Antankarana Kingdom (1690-1541 AD)
description: Located in the northernmost tip of Madagascar, the Antankarana Kingdom emerged around 1690. The state is famous for its fierce resistance against Merina expansion, with its people using the limestone Tsingy caves as natural fortresses. In 1841, facing imminent conquest by the Merina Empire, King Tsimiaro signed a protection treaty with France, effectively transitioning the kingdom from an independent state to a French protectorate to ensure survival.

name: Mauritius (1968-present)
description: After centuries as a Dutch, French, and British colony, Mauritius gained independence in 1968. Initially a Constitutional Monarchy under the British Crown, it transitioned to a Parliamentary Republic in 1992. Throughout its modern history, the island has transformed from a sugar-dependent colonial economy into one of Africa's most stable and prosperous democracies. Today, it remains a diverse nation with a unique heritage of enslaved and indentured labor, maintaining strong global financial and diplomatic ties.
